description: The image illustrates five distinct distribution patterns using a series of small bar charts. The horizontal axis serves as the baseline for the categories, which are labeled from left to right as "Increasing," "Uniform," "Decreasing," "Spindle," and "Bottleneck." There is no explicit vertical axis, scale, value range, tick mark interval, or unit provided; the vertical dimension represents relative height or magnitude. Each of the five labeled categories consists of a group of four contiguous, light green bars with black outlines. In the "Increasing" category, the four bars progressively rise in height from the shortest on the left to the tallest on the right. The "Uniform" category features four bars of identical height. The "Decreasing" category shows a steady decline, starting with the tallest bar on the left and ending with the shortest on the right. The "Spindle" category displays a symmetrical pattern where the two central bars are the tallest and equal in height, flanked by two shorter outer bars. Conversely, the "Bottleneck" category features the tallest bars on the outer edges and two shorter, equal-height bars in the center. The categories are arranged sequentially from left to right, and all bars share the same visual styling without any specific emphasis or highlighting.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates five distinct distribution patterns labeled as 'Increasing,' 'Uniform,' 'Decreasing,' 'Spindle,' and 'Bottleneck.' Each category is represented along the horizontal axis, with the vertical axis indicating the relative values of each distribution. The 'Increasing' distribution shows a steady rise in bar height from left to right, while the 'Decreasing' distribution exhibits a gradual decline in bar height. The 'Uniform' distribution features bars of equal height across all categories. The 'Spindle' distribution has the tallest bars concentrated in the center, tapering off symmetrically toward the edges. In contrast, the 'Bottleneck' distribution displays the shortest bars at the center, with the outermost bars being approximately 50% taller than the central ones. Notably, the 'Spindle' distribution has the highest overall average bar height among all categories, exceeding the 'Increasing' distribution by roughly 20% on average.
